cards.title: Introduction to Custom Hooks
cards.content:
Custom Hooks are JavaScript functions whose names start with use and that may call other Hooks. They allow you to extract component logic into reusable functions.

function useWindowWidth() {
  const [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth);
  // ...
  return width;
}

content.text: Custom Hooks must always start with the prefix '{{blank}}' and you should only call Hooks at the {{blank}} level.

cards.title: Extracting State Logic
cards.content: When you want to share logic between two JavaScript functions, you extract it to a third function. Both components and Hooks are functions, so this works for them too!

cards.title: Order the steps to create a Custom Hook

steps.text: Identify the duplicated stateful logic in components
Create a new function starting with the prefix 'use'
Move state and effect logic inside the new function
Return the necessary variables and functions from the custom hook

cards.title: Summary & Best Practices
cards.content: Custom Hooks improve code readability and maintainability. Remember that each *call* to a hook has a completely isolated state—sharing a custom hook shares only the logic, not the state itself.
